pages.headline: A site instruction changes the scope. The project manager opens drawings, email and the cost log to explain what happens next.
pages.body: A variation without its evidence. A handover missing accepted documents. A weekly commitment missed. An RFI answered elsewhere. Approved material without a delivery commitment. A delay event with a disputed chronology. Each needs the project record assembled, a decision made and an action owned. Orcaworks connects that work across project platforms, schedules, cost records and email.
pages.callout: 50% of respondents named delay claims as the main issue raised in construction disputes
pages.calloutSource: RIBA Survey (2022), via Global Arbitration Review

pages.eyebrow: 01 / Commercial · Scope change to approved position
pages.title: Change evidence to decision
pages.problem: A revised drawing, site instruction or unexpected condition changes the work. The project manager has to connect the original scope, trade quote, daily records, schedule activities and notice history before commercial review. Evidence sits across the project platform, email and cost log while affected work and potential exposure keep moving.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks assembles a source-linked change case, identifies missing proof and prepares the scope, cost and schedule questions. Project and commercial leaders approve the contractor position; owner-controlled changes follow the owner’s approval process before approved records and communications advance.

pages.eyebrow: 02 / Handover · Received is not yet accepted
pages.title: Closeout readiness
pages.problem: Practical completion is approaching, but the turnover register still contains gaps. A subcontractor sends a generic manual, a warranty lacks the asset reference and an as-built set uses the wrong revision. The closeout coordinator rechecks specifications and chases vendors while the owner’s acceptance, final payment and retention remain unresolved.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks reconciles expected, received and accepted deliverables by trade and asset, then prepares precise requests. Designers, commissioning teams and the owner accept the required evidence before the approved turnover register and handover status are updated.

rightContent.quote: Difficulty obtaining required documentation is a major cause of construction project closeout delays.
rightContent.source: Transportation Research Record · 2022 study of U.S. state DOT closeout practices

pages.eyebrow: 03 / Field delivery · Missed commitment to owned action
pages.title: Plan-versus-actual resolution
pages.problem: The weekly plan says a work area should be complete, but the latest field report shows a miss. The superintendent and planner search daily logs, delivery updates, open RFIs and submittals to establish the cause. By the coordination meeting, the team still needs an agreed explanation and a practical recovery action.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks connects the missed commitment to captured field evidence and its likely constraints. The superintendent and project manager choose the corrective action or resequencing, then the approved owner, due date and plan update are recorded.

rightContent.quote: Foundational LCI research found that only 54% of construction commitments were completed on time.
rightContent.source: Lean Construction Institute · Last Planner System

citation.text: Lean Construction Institute · Last Planner System

pages.eyebrow: 04 / Design coordination · Official answer to field distribution
pages.title: Cross-platform RFI continuity
pages.problem: The designer has answered an RFI in the owner’s platform, but the contractor’s register and trade team still show it open. The project engineer checks question IDs, drawing revisions, attachments and the response history, then works out which crews, change records and schedule activities need the approved answer before work proceeds.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks matches the official answer to the contractor’s RFI and affected records. The project engineer verifies the response and recipients; approved distribution and linked record updates follow, with technical interpretation remaining with the responsible designer.

pages.eyebrow: 05 / Materials · Technical approval to site commitment
pages.title: Submittal and procurement readiness
pages.problem: A submittal is approved, yet the material is not on track for the required installation date. Procurement checks the purchase order, release instruction, fabrication status and vendor emails while the planner compares the latest promise with the lookahead. Technical approval alone does not tell the superintendent whether the material will arrive.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks connects technical disposition, purchasing milestones and the vendor’s current commitment to the required site date. Procurement and project leaders approve expediting or resequencing; designers retain substitution approval, and the material-readiness record reflects the agreed action.

rightContent.quote: It’s not enough to find and implement a technology solution.

pages.eyebrow: 06 / Commercial review · Event record to defensible position
pages.title: Claims and delay chronology
pages.problem: A disputed delay or change requires a factual sequence months after the event. The commercial team rebuilds it from schedule updates, RFIs, daily records, meeting minutes, notices and correspondence. Conflicting dates and missing field proof must be resolved before the scheduler, commercial lead and counsel can assess the contractor’s position.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks prepares an event-specific chronology with source links, gaps and contradictory records. The scheduler validates program effects; commercial leaders and counsel decide notices, entitlement and strategy before an authorized chronology or communication is retained in the project record.

pages.title: Keep evidence, authority and action together
beforeItems: Change, schedule and site evidence sit in separate project records.
Teams reconstruct the event before each commercial or field decision.
Technical and commercial approvals are buried in messages.
Registers catch up after decisions and distribution are complete.
afterItems: A project-linked case brings the current evidence and open questions together.
The next step has an accountable owner and a defined completion state.
Designers, project leaders and owners retain their approval responsibilities.
Approved actions and accepted evidence return to the project records.
